findings.title: 7-neighbor benchmark target assigned by the plan entry is dropped
findings.description: The slice plan entry (140-slices.simulation-scaling.md:50) states: "the 7-neighbor operating point is a benchmark target." The design never mentions it; the gate config fixes `max_neighbors=32` and the walkthrough runs only that configuration. Per slice 148's rediagnosis notes (148-notes.rediagnosis.md), the early-exit gain scales with `candidates_scanned / max_neighbors`, so the 7-neighbor run is both plan-assigned and the highest-leverage data point — one extra bench invocation. Either add a `max_neighbors=7` benchmark run to the walkthrough/gates or record an explicit deferral with rationale.

findings.title: Gate workload `mid-flock-50k` does not match the stated N=50k operating point
findings.description: The design states "Default bench config for gate runs: `mid-flock-50k` workload" and gates A2/A3 at "N=50k". As committed, `bench/workloads/mid-flock-50k.yaml` specifies `n: 100000` and `world_size: [1536.0, 1536.0]` (internally inconsistent with its own description, which claims N=50k in a [400,400] world). The gate commands (lines 162–175) pass no N override, so as written the gates measure 100k agents at low density — not the dense N=50k two-flock regime the design's 45,000-candidate premise and occupancy analysis depend on. The gate spec should pin N and world size explicitly, or the workload file must be corrected before the gates are meaningful.

findings.title: Verification walkthrough targets a bench CLI surface that does not exist
findings.description: The walkthrough invokes `python scripts/bench.py --backend ... --config ... --N ... --ticks ... --parity-check ...`. The harness delivered by slice 141 is `python -m migratory.bench --workload <name> --backend <b>` (`src/migratory/bench/cli.py`); `scripts/bench.py` does not exist, the flag is `--workload` not `--config`, and no `--N`, `--ticks`, or `--parity-check` flags exist — N and tick counts are read from the workload YAML (`run(workload, args.backend, args.results_dir)`). `--subdivision-factor` is a new flag this slice plausibly adds, but the design's "No changes to" list (lines 103–106) and "Existing `quadrants-fused` backend API is unchanged externally" (line 80) do not scope any bench-harness surface changes, leaving the mechanism that runs the A1–A5 gates unspecified. Although the section is labeled "draft demo script", A2/A3/A5 acceptance depends on these runs. Specify the harness changes (new `--subdivision-factor` flag, parity-check entry, and how N/ticks are set per run) as in-scope, and correct the entry point and flag names to match the slice 141 harness.

findings.title: `cell_size` derivation placement misstated
findings.description: "The bench harness passes `cell_size` at setup; it reads from config" and the Component Interactions diagram (lines 85–86) place `cell_size` in BenchConfig. In fact `cell_size` is derived inside `GpuAgentState.setup()` as `max_query_radius * DEFAULT_CELL_SIZE_MULTIPLIER` (`quadrants_fused_state.py:150`) — it is not a config input today, and the derivation uses `max_query_radius` (max across profiles), not a single `query_radius`. The sibling task file (149-tasks, T2) already places the change correctly (`self.cell_size = self.max_query_radius / subdivision_factor`); the design doc should match so the single-source-of-truth constant and its "shared with the fused kernel" comment get updated deliberately.

findings.title: NFR restated with specific target
findings.description: The Success Criteria section restates the parent architecture's Tier 2 NFR (60 TPS at N=50k on CUDA) with the specific gate target (A3: ≥ 100 TPS, 1.67× headroom) and ties it to slice 146 sequencing. Matches the plan entry's exit criteria (≥5× force_total, ≥100 TPS, 20% parity) exactly.

findings.title: Scope and proportionality match the plan entry
findings.description: The two interventions (early exit at cap; configurable subdivision factor S with default 1) are exactly the plan entry's scope at the stated 2/5 effort. Distance-ranked k-nearest, GPU prefix sum, TickResult/world-server changes, and Metal tuning are correctly declared out of scope. Validation is explicit (config-time `ValueError`, hard error not silent clamp — consistent with project guidelines), the uncapped `max_neighbors ≤ 0` path is preserved via the `max_neighbors > 0` guard, and no new I/O paths or message types are introduced, so no additional failure-mode enumeration is required.

findings.title: Dependency direction and seam contracts preserved
findings.description: Depends on 145 only (matches plan entry); interface to 146 correctly asserts the `quadrants-fused` setup/tick API is unchanged so 146 stays unblocked. The Option A decision preserves the `get_neighbors_first_k` A7 swap point the plan requires both interventions to use. Code citations verified against `src/migratory/bench/backends/quadrants_fused_kernels.py`: seam at lines 155–184 (def at 156 under `@qd.func`), `for kk in range(start, end)` at line 291, and the stated Quadrants constraint (no `break` in the parallel outer loop, exit on the innermost loop) matches the kernel's structure and the slice 145 Phase 2.1 POC note. The generalized (2S+1)×(2S+1) scan preserves the neighborhood-coverage invariant (`cell_size = radius/S` makes the block cover exactly `query_radius`).
